messages:
mira (support): Heads-up: BrightSky reporting repeated 429s and p95 latency spikes on their EU2 dedicated pool since 09:10 UTC. They see saturation only on some nodes, not whole pool. Stack trace attached below.

mira (support): Observed behaviour: bursts of 429s for short windows (~30-90s), correlates with other tenants on same host. Customer is on reserved capacity so autoscale didn't engage.

omar (eng-sre): Can you paste the node-level metrics? GPU util, SMs, mem bw, and per-MIG slice stats if available.

mira (support): Pasted from node 10.4.3.21 around 09:12:
```
NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Persistence-M| Bus-Id        Disp.A | Volatile Uncorr. ECC |
|  0  A100-SXM4-80GB   On        | 00000000:3B:00.0 Off |                    0 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| MIG  Instance Profiles:
|  Slice  ID  SM%  Mem%  Enc%  Dec%
|  0      3   96    12    0     0
|  1      4   7     9     0     0
|  2      5   5     6     0     0
```

mira (support): App logs show KV cache misses spike at same time. Customer runs long-chat workloads (seq=2048 typical).

len (eng-runtime): That looks like one heavy slice hogging SMs while others starve. Could be kernel scheduling skews with our small-batch continuous batching logic. Any recent runtime change?

tara (eng-infra): No infra deploys in the window. We did a driver update last week but it was gradual. Hosts with same effect all on MIXED partitioning: some tenants have sidecar batchers enabled.

omar (eng-sre): Two quick repro steps to confirm: 1) Run a synthetic steady-state with few concurrent streams pinned to one MIG slice (seq 2048, batch size 1) and 2) run co-resident synthetic noisy worker with tiny kernels (short-latency inference) to try to trigger SM preemption.

mira (support): I ran (1) on isolated node and didn't see 429s; reproduced only on co-resident hosts. Customer provided tenant id ts-87431 and we confirmed they're on slice id 3 on that host.

len (eng-runtime): Hypothesis: our continuous-batcher may pack requests into the same worker process bound to the hot slice, causing KV cache pressure and L3 thrashing leading to occasional scheduler stalls + driver-level throttles -> 429s.

len (eng-runtime): Suggested mitigations: temporarily cap concurrency for ts-87431 to 8, move tenant to a different slice we know is lightly used, or enforce per-slice fairness in the runtime via a quick config toggle (disable aggressive pack on that pool).

tara (eng-infra): Quick mitigation applied: moved ts-87431 to slice 1 on host 10.4.3.24 and set concurrency cap rule for the account. We'll monitor for 10m.

deploy-bot: config-change: applied concurrency-cap for tenant ts-87431 by tara at 2026-03-17T09:20:45Z

omar (eng-sre): After move, do we see SM saturation drop on old host and p95 stabilize?

mira (support): Customer reports errors dropped to near zero within 2 minutes after migration. p95 returned to baseline. They thanked support.

len (eng-runtime): Follow-ups: 1) we should add a short-lived telemetry label on hosts to show per-slice sm_util and l3_pressure in the console, 2) create a canary to vary continuous-batcher packing policy on a small set of nodes to measure fairness regressions. I can put up a PR for the runtime change.

omar (eng-sre): Also recommend adding automatic throttling detector: if one slice's SM% > 85% while others < 20% for >30s, trigger a mitigation workflow (migrate or cap).

mira (support): Filing a customer postmortem and follow-up ticket to BrightSky with the actions taken and ask if they'd like a dedicated isolated slot long-term. Closing support loop now. :white_check_mark:
